X and Y Outputs ‘The DACs (011 and B11) each receive binary numbers from the vector generator’s pos!tion counters outputs. These numbers represent the location of the beam on the monitor. For the non inverted X axl, the numbers range from 0 to 1023, where Os at the far left of ‘the monitor screen, 512 atthe center, and 1023 is at the far right, For the non-inverted Y axis, the numbers range {rom 128 to 996, where 128 is at the bottom of the monitor Sereen, 61218 at the center, and 996 is atthe top. When the X axis and Y axis are inverted, tthe monitor picture is tured upside down. Ths is used for a two-player cocktail game. ‘The DACs convert these binary number inputs to current outputs. The DACs! current outputs are applied to the pin 6 Inputs of current-to-voltage converters C12 and A12.

From the current-iovoltage converter, the signal Is fed to two sample-and:nola cir cuits: One is nominverted and the other is inverted. The non-inverted sample and hold ‘consists of one stage of analog switch D12 and capacitor C98 for the X axis, and B12 and ‘C106 for the ¥ axis. The inverting sample and hold consists of inverter E12, one stage of ‘analog switch D12, and capacitor C119 for the X axis and B/C12, B12 and 118 for the Y axis,

‘The sample and hold circuits are controlled by SHCON (sample and hold contro). ‘SHCON is derived by gating 3 MHz from the microcomputer clock circuitry and VGCK* from the vector generator’s state generator. The result of these inputs insures that the ‘ominverted and inverted analog signals that are applied to the analog switches have sutficiently stabilized before being applied to the sample and hold capacitors.

‘The output swing of SHCON is 8 to +8 VDC. When SHCON is high, the voltage ‘charges oF discharges the sample-andhold capacitors to the X and Y analog voltage ‘value, The voltages are then applied to the inputs of the second analog switch. These ‘witches select ether the non-inverted or inverted Xaxis and Y-axis outputs. The outputs {are then amplified by the second stages of C12 and A12 for an impedance-matched out: put to the X and ¥ inputs to the monitor, Since the monitor doesn't have field-adjustable X and Y gains, the gains are adjustable by variable resistors R120 and R126.
